Chapter 3

1. Situational Hook

Every Island Has a Story

Setiap tempat punya cerita. Ada cerita yang berasal dari keluarga, kampung, pulau, laut, hutan, sekolah, atau pengalaman masyarakat. Cerita bisa membuat orang merasa takut, penasaran, terhibur, sedih, atau terinspirasi.

Di daerah kepulauan, misalnya, orang sering mendengar cerita tentang:

  • cahaya aneh di laut;
  • perahu yang pulang terlambat;
  • anak yang tidak mendengarkan nasihat orang tua;
  • nelayan yang bertemu makhluk misterius;
  • kura-kura yang terjebak tali rumput laut;
  • ikan emas yang bisa berbicara;
  • pulau kecil yang dianggap menyimpan rahasia;
  • seseorang yang serakah lalu mendapat akibatnya;
  • anak pemberani yang membantu orang lain.

Cerita seperti itu bisa dikembangkan menjadi narrative text.

Narrative text bukan hanya cerita “once upon a time”. Narrative text adalah cerita yang punya alur. Di dalamnya ada tokoh yang menghadapi masalah, lalu berusaha menyelesaikannya. Dari cerita itu, pembaca biasanya mendapat hiburan dan pelajaran.

Think First

Sebelum belajar, pikirkan pertanyaan ini:

  1. Cerita rakyat atau dongeng apa yang pernah kamu dengar?
  2. Siapa tokoh dalam cerita itu?
  3. Apa masalah yang terjadi?
  4. Bagaimana masalah itu selesai?
  5. Apa pesan moral dari cerita itu?
  6. Mengapa orang masih suka mendengar cerita lama?

2. Big Question

Pertanyaan besar bab ini:

How can we create an interesting story with clear characters, plot, conflict, and moral value?

Atau dalam Bahasa Indonesia:

Bagaimana kita bisa membuat cerita yang menarik dengan tokoh, alur, konflik, dan pesan moral yang jelas?

Chapter 3

3. Learning Objectives

Setelah mempelajari bab ini, siswa mampu:

  1. memahami isi narrative text sederhana;
  2. mengidentifikasi tokoh utama dan tokoh pendukung;
  3. menemukan setting tempat, waktu, dan suasana;
  4. mengidentifikasi masalah atau konflik dalam cerita;
  5. memahami urutan plot: beginning, rising action, climax, resolution, ending;
  6. menemukan struktur narrative text: orientation, complication, resolution, dan coda;
  7. membedakan narrative text dengan recount text;
  8. menggunakan simple past tense dalam cerita;
  9. menggunakan action verbs untuk menunjukkan aksi tokoh;
  10. menggunakan saying verbs untuk dialog;
  11. menggunakan adjectives untuk menggambarkan tokoh, tempat, benda, dan suasana;
  12. menggunakan time connectives untuk menyusun alur;
  13. memahami pesan moral dari cerita;
  14. menceritakan kembali cerita dengan kata-kata sendiri;
  15. membuat karakter dan konflik sendiri;
  16. menulis narrative text sederhana;
  17. mempresentasikan cerita secara lisan, visual, atau digital.
Chapter 3

4. What Is Narrative Text?

Narrative text adalah teks yang menceritakan sebuah cerita. Cerita itu bisa berupa cerita imajinatif, cerita rakyat, legenda, fabel, dongeng, mitos, cerita fantasi, atau petualangan.

Tujuan utama narrative text adalah:

to entertain the readers and often teach a moral lesson.

Artinya:

untuk menghibur pembaca dan sering kali memberikan pesan moral.

Simple Definition

Narrative text is a story text.
It tells about characters who face a problem and try to solve it.

Example

A boy saw a strange light near the sea. He wanted to follow it, but his grandmother warned him. In the end, he learned to be careful.

Dalam contoh pendek itu sudah ada:

Element Example
Character a boy, his grandmother
Setting near the sea
Problem he wanted to follow a strange light
Resolution he listened to his grandmother
Moral value be careful

5. Types of Narrative Text

Type Meaning Example
Folktale cerita rakyat A local story from an island
Fairy tale dongeng ajaib Cinderella
Fable cerita hewan dengan pesan moral The Tortoise and the Hare
Legend legenda asal-usul tempat/tokoh The Legend of Lake Toba
Myth cerita mitos/kepercayaan A story about a sea spirit
Fantasy story cerita imajinatif The Blue Lantern
Adventure story cerita petualangan A Boy and the Lost Boat
Moral story cerita dengan pesan moral The Honest Boy
Local tale cerita lokal The Light near Sapuka Caddi
Animal tale cerita hewan The Turtle and the Seaweed Rope
Chapter 3

6. Narrative Text vs Recount Text

Karena sebelumnya siswa belajar personal recount text, penting untuk membedakan recount dan narrative.

Aspect Recount Text Narrative Text
Purpose To retell past experience To entertain and teach moral value
Content Personal real experience Story, fantasy, folktale, fable, legend
Main focus What happened to the writer Character, problem, conflict, resolution
Structure Orientation, events, reorientation Orientation, complication, resolution, coda
Example My Trip to Makassar The Boy and the Blue Lantern
Ending Feeling or lesson from experience Moral value from the story

Simple Difference

Recount:

I went to the beach last Sunday.

Narrative:

Long ago, a boy found a magical shell near the beach.

Chapter 3

7. Social Function

Narrative text digunakan untuk:

  1. menghibur pembaca atau pendengar;
  2. menceritakan peristiwa imajinatif atau cerita rakyat;
  3. menyampaikan nilai moral;
  4. memperkenalkan budaya dan cerita lokal;
  5. melatih siswa memahami plot, karakter, dan konflik;
  6. mengembangkan imajinasi dan kemampuan bercerita;
  7. membantu siswa belajar sebab-akibat dalam cerita;
  8. mengajarkan nilai seperti kejujuran, keberanian, kesabaran, dan kepedulian.

Narrative in Real Life

Situation Narrative Use
Dongeng sebelum tidur Menceritakan cerita dengan pesan moral
Cerita rakyat daerah Mengenalkan budaya lokal
Film atau animasi Menampilkan tokoh, konflik, dan penyelesaian
Novel/cerpen Menghibur pembaca
Drama kelas Memerankan karakter dalam cerita
Komik Menampilkan plot melalui gambar
Video pendek Mengubah cerita menjadi visual
Podcast/audio story Menceritakan cerita dengan suara
Tugas Bahasa Inggris Menulis cerita imajinatif sederhana
Chapter 3

8. Generic Structure of Narrative Text

Narrative text biasanya memiliki empat bagian.

Structure Function Example
Orientation Mengenalkan tokoh, tempat, dan waktu Long ago, a young fisherman lived on a small island.
Complication Menunjukkan masalah atau konflik One night, his boat was carried away by strong waves.
Resolution Menjelaskan bagaimana masalah diselesaikan He followed the stars and finally returned home safely.
Coda / Moral Value Menyampaikan pesan moral atau penutup cerita From that day, he learned to listen to advice.

Simple Formula

Orientation

Who was in the story?
Where did the story happen?
When did it happen?
What was the character like?

Complication

What problem happened?
Why was it difficult?
How did the character feel?
What made the situation worse?

Resolution

How was the problem solved?
Who helped the character?
What happened at the end?

Coda / Moral Value

What lesson can we learn?
How did the character change?

9. Plot in Narrative Text

⛰️
Interactive Plot BuilderClick the story cards in the correct order. Build the plot mountain.
1Beginning
2Problem
3Rising Action
4Climax
5Resolution
6Moral

Plot adalah alur cerita. Plot menunjukkan urutan kejadian dari awal sampai akhir.

Narrative text yang baik tidak hanya berisi kejadian acak. Ceritanya harus bergerak dari awal, menuju masalah, lalu menuju penyelesaian.

Simple Plot Map

Part Question Example
Beginning Who? Where? When? A boy lived near the sea.
Problem What went wrong? He saw a strange light on the water.
Rising Action What happened next? He followed the light and lost his way.
Climax What was the most tense moment? A big wave came toward his boat.
Resolution How did it end? He remembered his father’s advice and returned home.
Moral What lesson did he learn? Do not act too quickly when you are afraid.

Plot Mountain

  1. Beginning
    The story starts normally. The reader meets the character and setting.

  2. Problem Begins
    Something unusual, difficult, or dangerous happens.

  3. Rising Action
    The problem becomes bigger. The character must make choices.

  4. Climax
    The most exciting, dangerous, or emotional moment.

  5. Resolution
    The problem is solved.

  6. Moral Value
    The story gives a lesson.

Example Plot Mountain

Title: The Boy and the Blue Lantern

Plot Stage Story Event
Beginning Rafi lived near a small pier.
Problem Begins He saw a blue lantern floating above the sea.
Rising Action He wanted to follow it.
Climax His grandmother stopped him and warned him.
Resolution He waited until morning and saw dangerous waves.
Moral Value Be brave but careful.

10. Character in Narrative Text

🎭
Character Role CardsClick a card to reveal how the role works in a story.

Character adalah tokoh dalam cerita. Tokoh membuat cerita hidup.

Cerita yang baik biasanya memiliki tokoh yang:

  • memiliki sifat tertentu;
  • menghadapi masalah;
  • membuat keputusan;
  • mengalami perubahan;
  • belajar sesuatu.

Types of Characters

Character Type Meaning Example
Main character tokoh utama The boy, the princess, the fisherman
Supporting character tokoh pendukung The mother, the friend, the old man
Antagonist tokoh lawan/penyebab konflik The greedy man, the monster
Helper tokoh penolong The wise grandmother, the turtle
Magical character tokoh ajaib A talking fish, a sea spirit
Narrator pencerita The person who tells the story

Character Traits

Trait Indonesian Example Sentence
brave berani The boy was brave.
kind baik hati The girl was kind to everyone.
wise bijaksana The old man was wise.
greedy serakah The merchant was greedy.
lazy malas The young man was lazy.
honest jujur The student was honest.
patient sabar The mother was patient.
clever pintar/cerdik The mouse deer was clever.
careless ceroboh The boy was careless.
helpful suka menolong The fisherman was helpful.
selfish egois The king was selfish.
humble rendah hati The girl was humble.
curious penasaran The child was curious.
frightened ketakutan The villagers were frightened.
lonely kesepian The old woman was lonely.
loyal setia The dog was loyal to its owner.
jealous iri The brother was jealous.
generous dermawan The queen was generous.
arrogant sombong The prince was arrogant.
responsible bertanggung jawab The boy became responsible.
careless ceroboh The child was careless near the sea.
respectful hormat The girl was respectful to her grandmother.

Character Change

Dalam narrative text, tokoh sering berubah.

Beginning Ending
careless careful
greedy generous
afraid brave
selfish helpful
lazy hardworking
dishonest honest
arrogant humble

Example:

At first, Lando was greedy. In the end, he learned to share with others.

11. Setting in Narrative Text

Setting adalah latar cerita.

Setting terdiri dari:

  1. Place — di mana cerita terjadi;
  2. Time — kapan cerita terjadi;
  3. Atmosphere — suasana cerita.

Setting Vocabulary

Category Vocabulary
Time long ago, once upon a time, one day, one night, in the morning, at sunset, during the storm, many years ago
Place in a village, on a small island, near the beach, in the forest, at the pier, on a boat, under a big tree, inside a cave
Atmosphere dark, quiet, peaceful, scary, mysterious, windy, stormy, bright, magical, dangerous, lonely, strange

Setting Examples

  • Long ago, there was a small village near the sea.
  • One night, the wind was strong and the sky was dark.
  • The story happened on a quiet island.
  • The forest looked mysterious at night.
  • The old pier was silent under the moonlight.
  • The sea became rough and dangerous.
Chapter 3

12. Conflict in Narrative Text

Conflict adalah masalah dalam cerita. Tanpa konflik, cerita biasanya terasa datar.

Conflict membuat pembaca bertanya:

What will happen next?

Types of Conflict

Type Explanation Example
Character vs Self Tokoh melawan rasa takut/keinginan sendiri A boy wanted to follow a strange light but felt afraid.
Character vs Character Tokoh berhadapan dengan tokoh lain A greedy man tried to steal the golden fish.
Character vs Nature Tokoh menghadapi alam A fisherman faced a storm.
Character vs Society Tokoh menghadapi aturan/masyarakat A poor boy wanted to prove his honesty.
Character vs Supernatural Tokoh menghadapi hal ajaib/misterius A girl heard a voice from a magical shell.

Conflict Sentence Starters

  • The problem began when …
  • Suddenly, …
  • Unfortunately, …
  • The character did not know what to do.
  • The character felt afraid because …
  • The situation became worse when …
  • The biggest problem was …

13. Moral Value

Moral value adalah pesan atau pelajaran yang bisa dipetik dari cerita.

Narrative text sering berisi moral value.

Common Moral Values

Moral Value Indonesian
Be honest. Jujurlah.
Do not be greedy. Jangan serakah.
Listen to your parents. Dengarkan orang tuamu.
Help others. Tolonglah orang lain.
Be patient. Bersabarlah.
Be brave but careful. Beranilah tetapi tetap hati-hati.
Do not break your promise. Jangan mengingkari janji.
Respect nature. Hormati alam.
Think before you act. Berpikirlah sebelum bertindak.
Kindness brings goodness. Kebaikan membawa kebaikan.
Greed brings trouble. Keserakahan membawa masalah.
Wisdom is better than hurry. Kebijaksanaan lebih baik daripada terburu-buru.
Small kindness can make a big difference. Kebaikan kecil bisa membawa dampak besar.

14. Language Features

A. Simple Past Tense

Narrative text biasanya menggunakan simple past tense karena cerita sudah terjadi.

Pattern:

Subject + Verb 2 + Object/Complement

Examples:

  • The boy walked to the beach.
  • The girl found a golden shell.
  • The fisherman saw a strange light.
  • The villagers heard a loud sound.
  • The turtle helped the child.

B. Was / Were

Subject Past To Be Example
I / He / She / It was The night was dark.
You / We / They were The villagers were afraid.

Examples:

  • The sea was calm.
  • The child was frightened.
  • The houses were small.
  • The people were worried.
  • The old man was wise.
  • The waves were dangerous.

C. Action Verbs

Action verbs menunjukkan tindakan dalam cerita.

Verb 1 Verb 2 Meaning
walk walked berjalan
open opened membuka

D. Saying Verbs

Saying verbs digunakan dalam dialog.

Saying Verb Meaning Example
said berkata “Be careful,” said the mother.
asked bertanya “Where are you going?” asked the old man.
answered menjawab “I am going to the beach,” answered the boy.
shouted berteriak “Help me!” shouted the girl.
whispered berbisik “Do not follow the light,” whispered the grandmother.
replied membalas “I will remember your advice,” replied the boy.
warned memperingatkan “The sea is dangerous tonight,” warned his father.
cried menangis/berseru “Please help me!” cried the child.
promised berjanji “I will return,” promised the prince.
begged memohon “Please let me go,” begged the fish.
explained menjelaskan “This shell belongs to the sea,” explained the old woman.

E. Time Connectives

Time connectives membantu menyusun alur cerita.

Time Connective Meaning Example
once upon a time pada suatu waktu Once upon a time, there was a poor fisherman.
long ago dahulu kala Long ago, people lived near the forest.
one day suatu hari One day, the boy found a golden shell.
one night suatu malam One night, he heard a strange voice.
at first pada awalnya At first, the boy was afraid.
suddenly tiba-tiba Suddenly, the wind became stronger.
then kemudian Then, the girl opened the box.
after that setelah itu After that, she ran home.
later kemudian Later, the old man returned.
finally akhirnya Finally, the villagers were safe.
in the end pada akhirnya In the end, the boy learned a lesson.

F. Adjectives for Stories

Category Adjectives
Characters brave, kind, wise, greedy, lazy, honest, patient, clever, careless, helpful, selfish, humble, curious
Places dark, quiet, peaceful, crowded, mysterious, dangerous, beautiful, magical, lonely, remote, stormy
Feelings afraid, happy, sad, angry, worried, excited, surprised, relieved, ashamed, thankful, confused
Objects old, golden, broken, strange, magical, heavy, small, shiny, wooden, mysterious, powerful

G. Direct Speech

Narrative text sering memakai dialog.

Example:

“Do not follow the light,” said the grandmother.

Pattern:

“Speech,” said the character.

More examples:

  • “Help me!” shouted the girl.
  • “Please let me go,” begged the fish.
  • “I will remember your advice,” replied the boy.
  • “The sea is dangerous tonight,” warned his father.

16. Listening Section

Listening Text 1

“The Boy and the Blue Lantern”

Long ago, there was a boy named Rafi. He lived near a small pier on Sapuka Island. Rafi was curious and brave, but sometimes he acted too quickly.

One windy night, Rafi saw a blue lantern floating above the sea. The light moved slowly away from the pier. Rafi thought it was a sign from his father’s boat. He wanted to follow it, but his grandmother stopped him.

“Do not follow every light you see,” whispered his grandmother. “The sea can hide many secrets.”

Rafi felt disappointed, but he listened to her. The next morning, he went to the pier and saw big waves near the place where the light had appeared. He realized that following the lantern at night could be dangerous.

From that day, Rafi learned to be brave but careful.

Listening Tasks

A. Main Idea

What is the story mainly about?

B. Details

  1. Who was the main character?
  2. Where did Rafi live?
  3. What did he see one windy night?
  4. Who stopped him?
  5. What lesson did Rafi learn?

C. Inference

What does “The sea can hide many secrets” mean?

D. Character Analysis

  1. Was Rafi brave or careless? Explain.
  2. Was the grandmother wise? Why?

Listening Text 2

“The Turtle and the Seaweed Rope”

One afternoon, a girl named Dina helped her mother near the beach. They were tying seaweed seedlings to long ropes. Dina was tired and wanted to finish quickly.

Suddenly, she saw a small turtle trapped in an old rope near the shore. The turtle moved slowly and looked weak. Dina wanted to continue her work, but she felt sorry for the turtle.

She called her mother. Together, they untied the old rope carefully. After a few minutes, the turtle was free. It moved back to the sea.

Dina smiled. Her mother said, “Work is important, but kindness is also important.”

Dina learned that helping a small creature could make her heart feel peaceful.

Listening Tasks

  1. What was Dina doing near the beach?
  2. What did she find near the shore?
  3. Why did the turtle look weak?
  4. How did Dina and her mother help the turtle?
  5. What moral value can we learn from the story?
  6. What kind of person was Dina?
  7. Which sentence shows kindness?

Listening Text 3

“The Voice from the Old Well”

Long ago, there was a small village near the coast. In the middle of the village, there was an old well. People said that the well was strange because it never became dry, even during the dry season.

One afternoon, a boy named Arman walked near the well. He heard a soft voice calling his name. Arman was frightened, but he was also curious. He moved closer and looked into the well.

Suddenly, the voice said, “Do not waste water. One day, you will need it.” Arman ran home and told his mother. His mother reminded him that water was precious, especially on an island.

From that day, Arman never played with water carelessly. He told his friends to save water. When the dry season came, the villagers were thankful because they had used water wisely.

Arman learned that nature gives warnings in quiet ways.

Listening Tasks

  1. Where did the story happen?
  2. What was strange about the old well?
  3. What did Arman hear?
  4. What message did the voice give?
  5. What did Arman learn?
  6. What moral value fits the story?

17. Speaking Section

A. Asking About Stories

Question Answer
What is the title of the story? The title is “The Boy and the Blue Lantern.”
Who is the main character? The main character is Rafi.
Where did the story happen? It happened near the pier.
When did the story happen? It happened one windy night.
What problem did the character face? He wanted to follow a strange light.
Who helped the character? His grandmother helped him.
How did the story end? He listened to his grandmother and stayed safe.
What is the moral value? We must be brave but careful.

B. Dialogue Practice 1 — Talking About a Story

Alya: What story did you read?
Rafi: I read “The Turtle and the Seaweed Rope.”
Alya: Who was the main character?
Rafi: The main character was Dina.
Alya: What problem did she find?
Rafi: She found a turtle trapped in an old rope.
Alya: What did she do?
Rafi: She helped the turtle with her mother.
Alya: What lesson did she learn?
Rafi: She learned that kindness is important.

C. Dialogue Practice 2 — Retelling a Story

Dina: Can you retell the story?
Salim: Yes. Long ago, there was a boy named Rafi.
Dina: Where did he live?
Salim: He lived near a small pier.
Dina: What happened one night?
Salim: He saw a blue lantern above the sea.
Dina: Did he follow it?
Salim: No, he did not. His grandmother stopped him.
Dina: What is the moral value?
Salim: We should think before we act.

D. Dialogue Practice 3 — Discussing Character

Teacher: What kind of character was Pak Sula?
Student: He was honest and patient.
Teacher: How do you know?
Student: Because he released the golden fish even though he was hungry.
Teacher: Good. What about the greedy man?
Student: He was selfish and greedy because he asked for gold and a big house.
Teacher: What lesson can we learn?
Student: We should not be greedy.

E. Speaking Mini Task

Retell a story in 1 minute.

Use this frame:

18. Reading Section

Reading Text 1 — Short

“The Greedy Boy and the Coconut Tree”

Long ago, there was a boy named Lando. He lived in a small village near the beach. Behind his house, there was a tall coconut tree. The tree gave many coconuts every month.

Lando’s mother always told him to share the coconuts with their neighbors. At first, Lando listened to her. But one day, he became greedy. He hid the coconuts and sold them alone at the market.

That night, a strong wind came. The coconut tree fell and broke. Lando felt sad and ashamed. He told his mother the truth and apologized.

From that day, Lando learned not to be greedy.

Questions

  1. Who was the main character?
  2. Where did Lando live?
  3. What did his mother tell him to do?
  4. What mistake did Lando make?
  5. What happened to the coconut tree?
  6. What moral value can we learn?
  7. What kind of character was Lando at first?
  8. How did Lando change at the end?

Reading Text 2 — Medium

“The Girl Who Listened to the Waves”

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Mira. She lived on a quiet island with her grandmother. Mira was kind and curious. She liked sitting near the beach and listening to the sound of the waves.

One evening, Mira heard a strange sound from the sea. It sounded like someone calling for help. She wanted to run to the water, but her grandmother warned her, “Do not go alone when the sky is dark.”

Mira listened to her grandmother. She called two neighbors and brought a lantern. Together, they walked carefully to the shore. There, they found a young fisherman whose small boat was stuck between rocks.

The neighbors helped the fisherman move his boat. The fisherman thanked Mira because she did not ignore the sound. Mira felt relieved and happy.

She learned that bravery must go together with wisdom.

Questions

  1. Who was Mira?
  2. What did Mira like doing near the beach?
  3. What did she hear one evening?
  4. Why did her grandmother warn her?
  5. Who helped the fisherman?
  6. What lesson did Mira learn?
  7. What was the complication?
  8. What was the resolution?

Reading Text 3 — Longer

“The Old Net and the Golden Fish”

Long ago, in a small fishing village, there lived an old fisherman named Pak Sula. He was poor, but he was honest and patient. Every morning, he went to the sea with his old net. Sometimes he caught many fish, but sometimes he returned home with nothing.

One morning, Pak Sula threw his net into the sea and waited quietly. When he pulled the net, he saw a small golden fish inside it. The fish looked at him and spoke, “Please let me go. I am not an ordinary fish.”

Pak Sula was surprised. He had never heard a fish speak before. The golden fish promised to help him if he released it. Pak Sula thought for a moment. He was hungry, but he felt sorry for the fish. Finally, he opened the net and let the fish swim away.

That night, Pak Sula found a basket of rice and vegetables in front of his house. He knew it was a gift from the golden fish. He was thankful and shared the food with his neighbors.

A greedy man heard about the golden fish. The next day, he went to the sea and tried to catch it. When he caught the fish, he asked for gold and a big house. The fish became sad and disappeared. The greedy man returned home with an empty net.

Pak Sula learned that kindness brings goodness, but greed brings nothing.

Questions

  1. Who was Pak Sula?
  2. What kind of person was he?
  3. What did he catch one morning?
  4. Why did he release the golden fish?
  5. What gift did he receive?
  6. What did the greedy man ask for?
  7. What happened to the greedy man?
  8. What is the moral value of the story?
  9. Compare Pak Sula and the greedy man.
  10. Which character changed the story most? Explain.

Reading Text 4 — Local Fantasy

“The Magical Shell of Sapuka Caddi”

Long ago, there was a girl named Lina who lived near the shore. Every afternoon, she helped her mother collect shells and clean the small yard beside their house. Lina was kind, patient, and careful. She never took more shells than she needed.

One cloudy afternoon, Lina found a shiny shell under a rock near Sapuka Caddi. The shell was small, but it glowed with a soft blue light. Lina wanted to keep it because it was beautiful. Suddenly, she heard a tiny voice from inside the shell.

“Please return me to the sea,” said the voice.

Lina was shocked. She looked around, but no one was there. At first, she was afraid. Then, she remembered her mother’s advice: “Do not take everything from nature. Some things belong to the sea.”

Lina walked slowly to the shore and placed the shell back into the water. The blue light disappeared under the waves. The next morning, Lina’s father found many small fish near his boat. Her family was thankful.

From that day, Lina learned to respect nature. She understood that kindness to the sea could bring goodness to people.

Questions

  1. Who was Lina?
  2. Where did she find the magical shell?
  3. What made the shell special?
  4. What did the shell ask Lina to do?
  5. Why did Lina return the shell to the sea?
  6. What happened the next morning?
  7. What moral value can we learn?
  8. Identify the orientation, complication, resolution, and coda.

Reading Text 5 — School Moral Story

“The Honest Student and the Lost Wallet”

One day, a student named Amir found a brown wallet near the school yard. He opened it and saw some money, an identity card, and a small family photo. Amir was surprised. He wanted to buy a new pen because his pen was broken, but he knew the wallet was not his.

Amir brought the wallet to the teacher’s office. His teacher asked him where he found it. Amir answered honestly, “I found it near the school yard, Ma’am.”

Later, a visitor came to the school and asked about a lost wallet. The teacher returned the wallet to him. The visitor was very happy because the wallet contained important documents. He thanked Amir and praised him for his honesty.

Amir felt proud, not because he received praise, but because he did the right thing. From that day, his friends respected him more.

The story teaches us that honesty is more valuable than money.

Questions

  1. What did Amir find?
  2. Where did he find it?
  3. What was inside the wallet?
  4. Why did Amir bring it to the teacher’s office?
  5. How did the visitor feel?
  6. What is the moral value?
  7. What would happen if Amir kept the wallet?

21. Common Mistakes

Mistake Correction Explanation
The boy see a light. The boy saw a light. Narrative memakai Verb 2.
The villagers was afraid. The villagers were afraid. Villagers plural, pakai were.
She did not followed the light. She did not follow the light. Setelah did not, pakai Verb 1.
The fish speak to him. The fish spoke to him. Speak menjadi spoke.
He was run to the beach. He ran to the beach. Jangan gabung was + Verb 1.
Finally he learn a lesson. Finally, he learned a lesson. Learn menjadi learned.
The boy was brave and follow the light. The boy was brave and followed the light. Verb harus konsisten bentuk lampau.
“Help me”! shouted the girl. “Help me!” shouted the girl. Tanda seru berada di dalam quotation mark.

C. Guided Writing Example

Title

The Magical Shell

Long ago, there was a girl named Lina. She lived in a small village near the beach. Lina was kind, patient, and helpful. Every afternoon, she helped her mother collect shells near the shore.

One day, Lina found a shiny shell under a rock. The shell was small, but it glowed softly. Suddenly, she heard a voice from inside the shell. “Please return me to the sea,” said the voice. Lina was surprised and afraid.

At first, she wanted to keep the shell because it was beautiful. However, she remembered her mother’s advice: “Do not take everything from nature.” Lina walked to the shore and put the shell back into the water.

The next morning, Lina found many small fish near her family’s boat. Her mother smiled and said that kindness to nature brings goodness.

From that day, Lina learned to respect nature and not to be greedy.

D. Stronger Example Text

“The Lost Boat and the Morning Star”

Long ago, there was a young fisherman named Hamzah. He lived on a small island with his father. Hamzah was brave, but he was also careless. He often went to the sea without checking the weather.

One afternoon, his father warned him, “Do not go too far today. The wind will be strong tonight.” Hamzah nodded, but he did not really listen. He took his small boat and went farther than usual because he wanted to catch more fish.

At first, the sea was calm. Then, dark clouds appeared in the sky. Suddenly, a strong wind pushed his boat away from the island. Hamzah tried to row back, but the waves became bigger. He felt frightened and remembered his father’s words.

In the middle of the dark sea, Hamzah saw a bright morning star. He remembered that his father once taught him how to use the stars to find direction. Slowly, he followed the star and rowed carefully. After a long night, he finally saw the island again.

When Hamzah arrived home, he apologized to his father. From that day, he learned that bravery without wisdom could bring danger.

“The Honest Boy and the Lost Bag”

Long ago, there was a boy named Amir. He lived in a small village near the sea. Amir was poor, but he was honest and kind.

31. Assessment Rubric

A. Writing Rubric

Aspect Excellent Good Needs Support
Structure Orientation, complication, resolution, and moral value are clear Most parts are clear Structure is confusing
Plot Story has clear beginning, problem, climax, and ending Plot is understandable Plot is weak or unclear
Character Character is well described and shows development Character is mentioned but simple Character is unclear
Setting Setting is clear and supports the story Setting is mentioned Setting is missing/unclear
Grammar Simple past mostly accurate Some grammar errors Many grammar errors
Vocabulary Uses varied action verbs, adjectives, and saying verbs Uses basic vocabulary Very limited vocabulary
Dialogue Dialogue is used naturally Dialogue is simple No dialogue
Moral Value Moral value is clear and meaningful Moral value is simple No clear moral value
Mechanics Good punctuation and capitalization Some mistakes Many mistakes

B. Speaking Rubric

Aspect Excellent Good Needs Support
Content Story is clear and complete Story is understandable Story is too short/confusing
Plot Sequence Events are told in good order Some order is clear Events are not organized
Pronunciation Clear and easy to understand Some unclear words Difficult to understand
Expression Good intonation and expression Some expression Flat voice/no expression
Confidence Confident and natural Fairly confident Very hesitant
Non-verbal Good eye contact, posture, and gesture Some eye contact/gesture Reads fully/no eye contact
Moral Value Moral value is clearly explained Moral value is mentioned Moral value is missing

C. Reading Rubric

Aspect Excellent Good Needs Support
Main Idea Identifies story idea clearly Identifies with minor help Cannot identify main idea
Character Identifies character and traits Identifies character only Cannot identify character
Plot Identifies problem and resolution Identifies some plot parts Plot understanding is weak
Moral Value Explains moral value clearly Mentions moral value Cannot explain moral value
Evidence Gives evidence from text Gives simple answer No evidence

32. Teacher Notes

Untuk siswa beginner–elementary:

  1. Mulai dari cerita pendek dengan plot sederhana.
  2. Gunakan gambar berseri untuk membantu siswa memahami alur cerita.
  3. Ajarkan tokoh, setting, masalah, dan solusi dengan bahasa sederhana.
  4. Jangan langsung menuntut cerita panjang.
  5. Gunakan pola:
    • character;
    • setting;
    • problem;
    • solution;
    • moral value.
  6. Siswa boleh menulis cerita lokal yang terinspirasi dari kehidupan pulau.
  7. Cerita rakyat atau mitos lokal harus diperlakukan sebagai cerita/kepercayaan masyarakat, bukan fakta ilmiah.
  8. Latih siswa memakai simple past tense melalui verb list.
  9. Latih retelling sebelum writing.
  10. Untuk speaking, siswa bisa mulai dari pair work, lalu small group, lalu presentasi kelas.
  11. Jika siswa kesulitan membuat cerita, berikan story starter.
  12. Jika siswa lemah grammar, fokuskan dulu pada plot dan makna cerita.
  13. Jika siswa sudah mampu, tambahkan dialog dan deskripsi suasana.
  14. Gunakan cerita lokal dengan hati-hati: bingkai sebagai folktale/local belief, bukan fakta ilmiah.
Chapter 3

33. Story Starters

Siswa dapat memilih salah satu pembuka cerita berikut.

  1. Long ago, there was a boy who lived near the sea.
  2. One night, a girl heard a strange voice from the beach.
  3. Once upon a time, an old fisherman found a golden fish.
  4. Many years ago, a small village had a mysterious well.
  5. One day, a student found a lost bag near the school yard.
  6. Long ago, a turtle was trapped in an old rope.
  7. One windy night, a blue lantern appeared above the sea.
  8. Once, there was a greedy boy who refused to share.
  9. One afternoon, a girl found a magical shell.
  10. Many years ago, a fisherman forgot his father’s advice.
Chapter 3

34. Useful Story Endings

  1. From that day, he learned to be careful.
  2. She learned that kindness brings goodness.
  3. The villagers learned to respect nature.
  4. He finally understood that greed brings trouble.
  5. In the end, honesty brought him respect.
  6. From that moment, she never ignored good advice.
  7. The story teaches us to think before we act.
  8. The moral value is: be brave but careful.
  9. The character learned that small kindness matters.
  10. The ending reminds us to listen to wise people.
Chapter 3

35. Summary of Chapter 3

Skill What Students Learn
Listening Understand simple narrative stories
Speaking Retell a story orally
Reading Identify characters, setting, problem, resolution, and moral value
Viewing Use picture story to understand plot
Writing Write narrative text with plot and characters
Presenting Present or retell a story
Grammar Simple past tense, action verbs, saying verbs
Vocabulary Characters, setting, problems, resolutions, moral values
Digital Literacy Turn story into caption, comic script, audio story, or short video script
